req.title: Update only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to update a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that a non-author user attempting to POST to /<id>/update must receive HTTP 403. We need: (1) a positive case confirming the author CAN update (HTTP 302 redirect on success), (2) a negative case confirming a non-author gets HTTP 403, and (3) a boundary case testing the exact post id boundary (post id=1 exists, post id=0 does not) to ensure the 403 vs 404 distinction is correct. Additional tests cover the state-transition (logged-in non-author) and decision-table (author vs non-author) dimensions. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (403, not >=400), exact redirect locations, and testing both sides of the author-check comparison.

tests.name: test_non_author_update_post_returns_403
preconditions: Database contains post id=1 authored by user id=1 (username='test')
User 'other' (id=2) is logged in via POST /auth/login
User 'other' is NOT the author of post id=1
actions: POST to /1/update with title and body form data
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_non_author_update_post_returns_403():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'hacked title', 'body': 'hacked body'})
    assert r.status_code == 403

test_non_author_update_post_returns_403()
